passages.title: New Year celebrations
passages.instructions: Read the story and answer the questions (41–50) according to the information in the story.
paragraphs: Millions of people in the world celebrate New Year. It is also celebrated in our country on the 1st of January. This day is a national holiday. We express our best wishes to our families and friends who live inside and outside Eritrea. We also exchange postcards and other gifts with our best friends to share our happiness.

[line 5] Of all New Year celebrations, the Chinese New Year is the longest. The Chinese don’t use European calendar. They have their own traditional calendar. Therefore their New Year begins sometime between 21 January and 20 February. It is celebrated for two weeks.

Chinese New Year begins by families visiting each other. It is a time for visiting friends [line 10] and relatives. They pay back money if they have borrowed any. They buy new clothes and give gifts. Children are also given ‘lucky’ money in red envelops, and coins are shaken from a ‘money’ tree to bring good luck.

At New Year people eat only vegetarian meals which contain no meat. This is because they give animal names to each New Year, for example, the Year of the Rat, the Year of [line 15] the Tiger, and so on. The most delicious type of food Jiaoz is cooked on this day. It is a small ball of white flour which has money, gifts or good luck messages inside. Some of the food is left in the kitchen for the spirit of the dead people to eat alone so that they will have a Happy New Year too.

On New Year’s Day the people go into the street to celebrate. They wear beautiful [line 20] traditional clothes, and there are people marching with flags, flowers and fireworks. The most enjoyable thing is the dance played with a white- coloured model of a dragon or lion. This big animal moves through the streets to the music of drums and seems to come alive when the dancers twist and turn. Towards the end of the celebrations, the streets are lighted with colourful lights to welcome the longer warmer days after the dark and cold winter.
passages.note: The paper gives no title. Line numbers (5–20) as printed. Bold in the questions: It (line 15), vegetarian (line 13).

questions.stem: When do the Chinese people celebrate New Year?

options.B: They celebrate on the 1st of January.
options.C: They celebrate on the European calendar.
options.D: They celebrate sometime between 21 of January and 20 of February.

questions.stem: Chinese children are given ______

options.A: money in envelops and coins from a ‘money’ tree.
options.B: delicious food which has money or gift inside.
options.C: new fashionable cars and clothes by friends and relatives.
options.D: flags of their country and different colours of flowers.

explanation_steps: “Children are also given ‘lucky’ money in red envelops, and coins are shaken from a ‘money’ tree.”
Textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons (e.g. Unit 10, p. 199–220: stories).
questions.explain_simple: Children get money in red envelopes and coins.

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is true?

options.A: The Chinese use European calendar to celebrate New Year.
options.B: The Chinese celebrate New Year on 21 January and 20 February.
options.C: People pay back money on New Year.

explanation_steps: “They pay back money if they have borrowed any.” → C true.
A false (own calendar). B false (sometime BETWEEN those dates, not on both).
questions.explain_simple: They pay back money at New Year.

similar_questions.stem: Which is true?

options.A: The Chinese eat meat at New Year.
options.B: The Chinese eat only vegetarian meals at New Year.

textbook_ref.rule: A 'true' statement must agree with the text in every part; the text may say it in other words.
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons

questions.stem: What does “It” (line 15) refer to?
explanation_steps: “The most delicious type of food Jiaoz is cooked on this day. It is a small ball of white flour …”
tips: Look at the noun just before.

questions.stem: What does “vegetarian” (line 13) mean?

options.A: A person who eats only vegetables
options.B: A person who eats only meat
options.C: A person who eats both vegetable and meat
options.D: A person who only eats rats and tigers

explanation_steps: The text explains: “vegetarian meals which contain no meat”.
A vegetarian eats no meat, only vegetables (plant food).
Textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227.
tips: Look for an explanation right after the word (“which contain no meat”).

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is false?

options.A: The people of China wear traditional clothes on New Year.
options.B: The people dance in the streets with a white-coloured model of a dragon or lion.
options.C: Big animals like lions come from the zoo to dance with the people.
options.D: Lights are lighted in the streets to welcome the longer warm days.

explanation_steps: The dragon or lion is a MODEL moved by dancers, not a real animal from a zoo. C is false.
questions.explain_simple: The lion is a model, not a real animal. C is false.

questions.stem: The people of China become so happy in the streets to see ______

options.A: the people dance with traditional clothes and march with flags and flowers.
options.B: the model of the big animal moves through the streets.
options.C: the streets lighted with different clourful lights.

explanation_steps: “The most enjoyable thing is the dance played with a white-coloured model of a dragon or lion. This big animal moves through the streets …”
So the thing that makes people happiest is the model animal moving through the streets.
Textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons (e.g. Unit 10, p. 199–220: stories).
questions.explain_simple: The most enjoyable thing is the dragon or lion dance.
